production.note: US model years. First: Edmunds lists the 2005 DB9 '2dr Coupe (5.9L 12cyl 6M)' and '(6A)' at '450 hp @ 6,000 rpm'; Aston's launch release (supercars-db9-release) gives a US price of '$163,900'. Last: Edmunds' 2013 review (edmunds-db9-2013-review) says 'The 2013 Aston Martin DB9 receives a significant refresh ... the engine and chassis greatly revised' with '510 horsepower', so 2012 is the last model year of this car; no opened page says '2012' in so many words. Car & Classic (carandclassic-db9-guide) dates the big 2012 update. UK build began early 2004.

body.note: 2+2 coupe. The DB9 Volante is sold under its own name and is not part of this record.

aspiration.note: 'quad-cam 48-valve' V12 with no turbocharger or supercharger.

drivetrain.note: 'Rear wheel drive'; Aston: 'The DB9 is fitted with a rear transaxle' (supercars-db9-release).

transmission.note: Aston: 'Two transmissions are offered: a six-speed ZF automatic gearbox and a new six-speed Graziano manual gearbox.' The automatic is Aston's Touchtronic. Car & Classic (carandclassic-db9-guide): 'By mid-2011, the manual gearbox was dropped'.

powerHp.note: Quote (Evo specification panel, 2004 DB9): "Power: 450bhp @ 6000rpm". Aston's launch release (supercars-db9-release): '450bhp and maximum torque 420lb ft'; Edmunds (edmunds-db9-2005) gives the US 2005 car '450 hp @ 6,000 rpm', so the US rating is the same figure. Reference year 2005: 450 hp applied to 2005-2008 and the 2008 Geneva update raised it to 470 bhp (Evo: 'a power upgrade to 470bhp'; Car & Classic: 'A further facelift in 2008 saw a power bump to 470 bhp'), i.e. 2009-2012 in the US. Each rating covers four of the eight model years, not more than half, so the launch rating is used.

weightLb.note: Step 2 of the weight order (major magazine specification panel; no Aston page with a weight could be opened). Quote (Evo specification panel, 2004 DB9): "Weight: 1760kg". 1,760 kg x 2.20462 = 3,880 lb. Evo does not say kerb or dry or which gearbox; Aston's coupe kerb weights were 'initially quoted 1710kg manual, 1760kg auto, later revised to 1760kg & 1800kg respectively' (AstonMartins.com, an enthusiast site, not cited), so 1,760 kg is the revised manual figure, i.e. the standard car. Car & Classic (carandclassic-db9-guide, no named author) gives '1760 kg (early)' for the coupe.

discrepancies.reason: Initial vs revised factory figures, and transmission. AstonMartins.com (enthusiast site, not cited): 'initially quoted 1710kg manual, 1760kg auto, later revised to 1760kg & 1800kg respectively'. 1,710 kg (3,770 lb) was the initial manual figure (no citable page gives it); Edmunds' 'Curb Weight: 3,968 lbs.' (1,800 kg), printed for both manual and automatic, is the revised automatic figure.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Evo's 1,760 kg, which matches the revised manual (standard car) figure.

discrepancies.reason: Supercars.net's specification table on the launch-release page prints 'curb weight | 1710 kg / 3770 lbs'; Evo's panel gives 1,760 kg.
discrepancies.resolution: Used Evo's 1,760 kg (a major magazine panel); Supercars.net's table is not the release text and is not attributed to Aston Martin.
